accounting_rules: All probability distributions are illustrative assumptions, not estimated from observed SYNERGY enterprises.
Annual growth draws represent cashflow after OPEX and before replacement CAPEX.
The correlated shock is a joint downside event applied to cashflow growth and replacement inflation in the same year.
Automation yield is drawn once per funded cohort and represents net residual after incremental OPEX and replacement.
R&D success is sampled independently across ten projects per annual cohort; failed projects produce zero return.
R&D yield is counted only after the deployment lag and only during the finite benefit life.
Positive residual is allocated 50/25/25; negative residual draws the reserve and then records an unfunded gap.
Reserve depletion probability means the reserve was exhausted at least once during the horizon, even if later contributions replenish it.
Monte Carlo results are conditional on the chosen distributions and must not be presented as real-world forecast probabilities.
